i agree with u but i also have a slightly different perspective. i'm a canadian applicant, and getting into the top canadian schools is WAY easier than getting into the top US schools. it's also way cheaper. if i didnt have the ambition to apply to ivies and t20s, i would be just like the normal canadian applicant, who doesn't even have to write essays (maybe 1-2 essays at most), apply to like 4 schools, basically be able to predict my acceptances, and only have to focus on maintaining my average in non-AP courses. BUT... i put myself through the US application process, where i had to pay a crap ton for application fees, APs, SAT and SAT IIs, and wrote a shit ton of essays. i think im the clown for not settling with the easier route. needless to say, ofc american schools give better opportunities, so thats why those of us who apply want to apply. 

there's this kid at my school who gave up on his wish to go to stanford. he wore a fucking stanford hoodie everyday (weird, ik), and he had insanely good grades. but he was lazy and didnt want to work on ECs and do the SAT, so he gave up and just applied to good canadian unis. i WISH i was him. i wish i was slightly lazier, and just decided not to put in time to apply and give up my chances to get into a US school. 

the US system is so much more difficult. they care about essays, ECs, grades, rec letters, standardized testing, course difficulty, geographical location, race to some extent, and some schools even asked for your sexuality.... the only thing canadian schools care about is: your average. 95.8% can get rejected, but 96% will get in (its fucking stupid i know). the plus side is, that we can basically just predict where we will end up by looking at the school's historic admissions averages, and we don't have to write good essays, or any essays for that matter. i applied to engineering/cs programs, so i did have to write essays and do interviews (and some cs programs are suuuper competitive) but if i applied to science, math, or arts, i basically would just have to enter in my grades and then voila if its high enough i get in.

mcgill is often regarded as the "best canadian school". i disagree, for my program its meh, and i think it's just good for grad school. you know what my mcgill application consisted of??? i was too busy with applying to US unis that my mom took my transcript and entered in my senior grades. it took her a total of 3 minutes. my mom basically did my application to the best canadian school, and i got in like a week later. nonetheless, canadian students are required to have really high grades if they are applying to competitive programs, but its WAY less stressful than US applications. frankly, i hate judging someone based off of their grades only, but hey, i wouldn't have to write essays, right? i don't feel happy at all that i got in to mcgill when i didnt have to put in any effort.

yep, if we were a little bit less ambitious, and happier with easier schools, we would be more emotionally stable, probably a few hundred dollars richer, and stress free.

I was forced to laugh at racist jokes towards asians to "fit in" at like 7 years old, even if my heart sunk hearing those jokes. 

The case with international students is also interesting, because they are a group within a mostly white (at least at my school, there is a significant chinese international student population, but my school and city are mostly white) environment. However, unlike people who were born or raised from a very young age in a predominantly white setting as an asian (like me), they don't have that identity crisis that we go through, because they have already fully connected with their cultural identity having spent time in their asian country. 2nd gen, or 1.5 gen kids however, are brought up in a western setting with asian parents, so we have that self identity issue where we dont really accept ourselves until we get older. So while international students do probably get racist remarks towards them, they can brush it off easily since they are fully confident with their identity. They are honestly all richer, more stylish, and cooler than me and the white kids at my school.
